Sampled-candidate ranking can disagree with full-catalog ranking, including reversing model comparisons in expectation; narrow confidence intervals do not remove this bias ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). RecSys 2025 research examines sampling reliability through model separability, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and agreement with ground truth ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086)). For this task, retain pinned validation HR@10 for selection; separately inspect each category’s single model on full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Without relevance labels, catalog coverage, popularity concentration and list overlap characterize behavior, not recommendation accuracy.

Evidence for diagnostic trustworthiness is less direct. A 2024 study revisits limitations of model-randomization sanity checks, cautioning against treating one perturbation test as definitive validation ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.06465)). Proposed adaptation for NextItNet: compare intact inference with controlled faults such as an incorrect padding readout, shuffled nonpadding history, or zeroed sequence features; use matched, function-preserving controls such as identical-input reruns and batch reordering. Predefine each probe’s expected response and check sensitivity to fault severity. These are suggested experiments, not established findings for this benchmark; order shuffling tests sequence dependence rather than automatically proving a defect.

For uncertainty, use a paired user-level bootstrap within each category, preserving each user’s candidate set and resampling identical users across comparisons. Bootstrap categories separately, then recompute their equal-weight macro average. Report intervals for HR@10 differences and diagnostic changes. Such intervals describe uncertainty conditional on these users, candidates and fitted models; they do not capture training-seed variation, repeated-search selection bias, or sampled-to-catalog bias. The targeted search found no directly matching 2024–2026 recommender study validating this entire diagnostic protocol.
